intuition: For each word, try splitting it into shorter dictionary words. Save which character boundaries can be reached by valid pieces. Reaching the end proves a split exists, but the original word alone must not count. Skip the transition that uses the entire candidate as one piece.

Treat character positions as boundaries. reachable[end] means the prefix ending immediately before end can be segmented. Begin with boundary zero, then try every earlier reachable start whose substring word[start:end] is a dictionary entry. This turns many repeated cut-pattern explorations into one dynamic-programming table per word.

The sole forbidden transition is using the entire candidate from boundary zero to its final boundary. Excluding it ensures that reaching the final boundary requires at least two pieces. All other dictionary entries can be reused, including entries that are themselves concatenated words. A set provides fast lookup, though Python still copies substring characters.
The original dictionary order does not matter because every candidate is tested against the full set rather than only earlier inputs.

steps: The example dictionary includes "cat", "cats", "dog", "rat", and several longer words. Build its membership set once.
"cat" and "cats" cannot reach their final boundary without the forbidden whole-word transition, so they are not emitted.
"hippopotamuses" has no valid shorter segmentation. Return the three concatenated entries.

codeNotes.note: The empty prefix establishes the first legal boundary from which a dictionary component can begin.
Skipping only the whole-candidate transition enforces the at-least-two-components requirement without removing useful dictionary entries globally.

approach: Begin with the empty boundary reachable.
Test dictionary pieces between earlier reachable boundaries and later boundaries.
Accept a word when its end is reachable through proper pieces.
concept.correctness: A reachable boundary means exactly that its prefix is a concatenation of dictionary pieces. Every extension preserves that meaning, and every valid construction supplies such a boundary sequence. Excluding the whole-word single piece ensures a reachable nonempty end uses at least two pieces. Thus the test accepts exactly concatenated words.

complexity.explanation: For each candidate, testing all boundary pairs is quadratic in length; copied substring checks can add another length factor. The dictionary and one candidate’s reachability table dominate extra storage.

pitfalls: The whole candidate alone must never count as its own construction.
